name: Mikel Morgan
strengths: Morgan wins with first-step get-off from a stand-up or hand-in-dirt look and turns the corner with a dipped shoulder on speed rushes.
Morgan chases scrambling quarterbacks sideline to sideline and finishes with closing burst after chips and across-the-field pursuit.
Morgan plays the ball after the rush: bats a throw at the line and dives on a loose snap in the backfield.
weaknesses: Morgan still wins mostly with speed and motor. Hand counters (swipe, club, rip) are raw once a tackle latches his chest.
Morgan plays high on some snaps and needs functional mass to set the edge and convert speed to power against college tackles.
comparison: Morgan comps to Kingsley Enagbare - listed 6-4 / 225 vs Enagbare's 6-4 long EDGE mold (same height, same lean rusher frame); then matching get-off, bend, and chase-first traits with power still to add (size-matched; not a Florida-alum default).
projection: Morgan projects to develop in Florida's EDGE room with Year-1 special-teams / scout-rush snaps, Year 2-3 compete for rush-package rotation, and starter ceiling if the speed rush adds mass and a hand plan.
schemeFit: Morgan fits a Brad White multiple front that wants a long JACK / wide-9 speed rusher who can stand up or put a hand down, chase, and grow a counter package.
staffNotes: FILM VERIFIED 2026-09-04 from Columbia HS sophomore end-of-season Hudl (Mikel Morgan, 2:36). Watched full package - get-off, bend, chase motor, bat, fumble recovery. Hands and pad level still polish. Comp size-matched within ~1-2" - not a Florida-alum default.
recruitingStory: Mikel Morgan is a 2028 EDGE listed 6-4 / 225 out of Columbia HS (Lake City, FL). 247 87 (Pos #57, FL #71). On3 national ranks blank. Florida offered Sept 2026. Bam Hardmon on the card. Uncommitted. UF RPM ~13%, FSU ~11%.
angle: Lead with Florida's new offer on the Lake City EDGE, then get-off / chase tape and Hardmon process.
insiderNotes: Morgan is a long 6-4 / 225 Columbia EDGE who wins with get-off, bend, and chase. He bats balls at the line and finishes loose plays in the backfield. Next step is hands and mass so the speed rush holds against college tackles.
